clue.text: Discerning kissing and petting?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: perceiving or managing to see something faintly
second meaning: a slang phrase for amorous fondling

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a judgement about canoodling, but the clue simply puts two senses of one phrasal verb side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To make out is to perceive dimly, and also informal slang for snogging, so the participle fits each half.

clue.text: Oddly, may very well cut short nonsense

indicators.note: cutting something short removes its tail, so the final letter goes
the odd-numbered positions are the ones kept, every other letter starting with the first

parts.note: letters one, three, five and so on of the run of three words

explanation.surface: Someone suspects a claim may very well be rubbish that ought to be trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: Take alternate letters of 'may very well' ignoring the spaces to get MYEYEL, then drop the last letter for MY EYE.
explanation.definitionFit: "My eye!" is a dated British exclamation of disbelief, used much like saying rubbish or poppycock.

clue.text: Lark around with rancid Boris, perhaps

indicators.note: to fool around is to move about aimlessly, so these letters wander out of order

parts.note: taken as written
food that has gone off is rancid

explanation.surface: A politician called Boris fools about with something that has gone rotten.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at Boris Johnson, but the Boris meant is the horror actor; 'perhaps' flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Karloff was the stage name of the actor famous for playing Frankenstein's monster in 1930s horror films.

clue.text: Language from north or south Spain

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north
taken as written
S is the compass abbreviation for south
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A question of which tongue is spoken in the northern or southern parts of Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word after 'from' gives a single abbreviation or itself; the Spanish setting is pure decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse is the old Scandinavian tongue of the Vikings, the ancestor of Norwegian, Icelandic and related speech.

clue.text: Working copy contained in press release, theoretically

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

indicators.note: something contained in another sits inside it, held within its outer letters

parts.note: PR is short for press release
to ape is to copy or mimic

explanation.surface: A draft of a press release is being worked on, at least in principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working copy' reads as one phrase about a draft document, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true on paper holds in principle or in the written plan but may not survive real practice.

clue.text: High quality portrait artist?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: of the finest class or standard
second meaning, whimsical: someone who sketches the upper half of a person, head and shoulders

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: a portraitist draws faces from the top, so is a drawer of tops.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer is an idiom for first-rate or socially superior, from the drawer where the best things are kept.

clue.text: Communication system for partners screened by Coca-Cola

indicators.note: what is screened is hidden behind something, so the letters lie concealed in the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first part and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A new messaging service for couples, sponsored by a fizzy drinks giant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partners' suggests couples, but it means bridge partners; Acol is a bidding system, the language partners use to tell each other about their hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Acol is the standard British bidding system in contract bridge, a coded method for partners to describe their cards.

clue.text: Can't be arsed keeping aardvark

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so the phrase holds the letters within it

parts.note: runs from the second letter of the first word into the start of the last

explanation.surface: Someone too lazy to bother looking after a pet aardvark.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored when reading through the letters. 'Can't be arsed' is British slang for being unable to summon the effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Antbear is another common name for the burrowing African mammal that feeds on termites and ants.

clue.text: Soft frame broken and inoperative

indicators.note: something broken is smashed into bits that can be put together differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A flimsy frame has collapsed and no longer works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft frame broken' reads like a description of the damage, while 'and inoperative' looks like more of the same, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant or machine off stream is not in production or service, the opposite of being on stream.

clue.text: Run quickly, then fall, producing sign of distress

parts.note: to tear along is to rush
to drop is to fall

explanation.surface: A child sprints, trips over, and starts to cry.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb 'tear' rhymes with 'bear' here, though in the answer it is the other word spelt the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A single falling tear is a visible symptom of sadness or upset, the classic outward mark of being upset.

clue.text: Excited to be back, posh boy discouraged

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so these letters run right to left

parts.note: someone excited is up, keyed up
toff is British slang for an upper-class person

explanation.surface: A public-school lad, keen to return home, has lost heart.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is a British word for a well-off, upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Being put off means deterred or made reluctant, a close phrasal synonym for losing enthusiasm.

clue.text: Writer is the first person in Paris and its Italian equivalent

parts.note: je is the French for I
Paris is the French capital, so the Italian counterpart is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: A boast that some author ranks top in Paris and likewise in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Its Italian equivalent' seems to want the Italian for I; in fact 'its' refers to Paris itself, so the Italian equivalent is another capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerome K. Jerome was the English author of the comic novel Three Men in a Boat.

clue.text: Bad omens from rector in powerful sermon's introduction

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, surrounded by the outer letters

parts.note: potent means powerful
R is a standard abbreviation for rector

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so only the very first letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A clergyman's forceful preaching opens with dire warnings of doom.
explanation.walkthrough: R for rector is a common abbreviation; it goes inside the word for powerful before the sermon's first letter is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Portents are signs foretelling something momentous, usually ominous, so they are warnings of coming calamity.

clue.text: Sustenance rejected by American idiot

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so its letters return in the opposite order

parts.note: food is sustenance
US is short for American, as in the US

explanation.surface: A foolish American refuses the food he is offered.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'American idiot' one phrase, but the nationality is a wordplay piece and the idiot stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Doofus is informal American slang for a stupid or clumsy person, a fool or dimwit.

clue.text: Briefly made errors performing military instruction

indicators.note: putting it briefly means cutting short, so the final letter is dropped
performing suggests a routine acted out, the letters put through their paces into new positions

parts.note: the word with its tail removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers on the parade ground briefly slipped up while carrying out drill.
explanation.walkthrough: Trim 'made' to three letters, then rearrange those with 'errors'.
explanation.definitionFit: Order arms is a drill command telling soldiers to bring the rifle down to rest upright beside the right foot.

clue.text: Trip in motor car is painful for Greens

parts.note: a spin is a short drive for pleasure
something that aches is painful

explanation.surface: A car journey is an ordeal for environmentalists, the Green Party.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital G makes 'Greens' look like the political party, but it is leafy vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green vegetable, so varieties of it are greens in the kitchen sense.

clue.text: Put into different part of hospital and remunerated?

definitions.text: Put into different part of hospital
definitions.meaning: first meaning, punning: placed in a ward again, a new one

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the first reading splits the word as re- plus warded, an invented verb for moving a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: To be rewarded is to receive payment or recompense for one's work or service.

clue.text: Caught venomous snake and established Australian city

indicators.note: to catch what someone says is to hear it, so these words are taken by ear

parts.note: an adder is Britain's poisonous snake and laid means established, as in laid down

explanation.surface: Someone caught a deadly snake and set up a city in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like grabbing the snake, but it means heard; in a non-rhotic accent the two words run together into the city name.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is the state capital of South Australia, named after Queen Adelaide.

clue.text: Fish with appendages for walking on

parts.note: legs are the limbs used for walking
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A strange fish that has legs to walk about on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like a preposition tacked to 'walking', but it is the definition: in cricket the on side is the half of the field behind a right-handed batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket uses on and leg side as interchangeable names for the same half of the field.

clue.text: Passage from additional court

parts.note: extra means additional
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A corridor leading off from an annexe courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' reads as a corridor, but the sense is a section of text.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a short section quoted from a book or document, as is a passage.

clue.text: Compete with me for cluster of flowers

parts.note: to race is to compete
taken as written

explanation.surface: A challenge to a rival gardener to vie for a prize bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is almost literal; the difficulty is knowing the botanical term.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a raceme is a flower spike with stalked blooms along a central stem, as in foxgloves or lupins.

clue.text: Man visiting India for local bread

parts.note: a chap is a man
someone visiting a place is at it
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tourist in India goes looking for the regional flatbread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' refers back to India in the surface, which is why that word can define an Indian bread fairly.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is an unleavened wholemeal flatbread from the Indian subcontinent, cooked on a griddle.

clue.text: Sweet-smelling old woman blocks men-only group from over the pond

indicators.note: something that blocks a channel sits inside it, plugging the middle

parts.words: men-only group from over the pond
parts.note: a frat is an American college fraternity, a male society; over the pond means in the US
gran is a grandmother

explanation.surface: A perfumed grandmother stands in the way of an all-male American club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over the pond' is British slang for across the Atlantic, so it signals an American word.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragrant describes anything with a pleasant scent, such as perfume or flowers, so it is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Reportedly spot one's flat under water

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: a spot is a location

explanation.surface: Rumour has it someone's apartment is flooded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's flat' looks like a home, yet 'one's' is just 'one is', and 'flat under water' is a flatfish; read it as 'spot is flat under water'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a European flatfish, so it is a flat creature living beneath the sea.

clue.text: Grumpy Londoner hides artificial leg

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it out of sight inside, so the letters are buried in the phrase

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A grouchy Londoner keeps a prosthetic limb out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual sense of the answer is an electricity tower, so the obscure sense of the definition is the hurdle.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists pylon as a dated term for a simple temporary prosthetic leg, a rare dictionary sense.

clue.text: Announced change is in store

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken out, so the word is judged by how it is said

parts.note: change is coins, money in hand

explanation.surface: A declaration that something new is coming, that change is in store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change is in store' is an idiom for something new on the way; here 'change' means coins and 'store' is a hoard.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden stockpile or reserve, so it is a store of goods kept aside.

clue.text: Spectre of violent anger covering Italy

indicators.note: a covering wraps around something, so outer letters surround an inner one

parts.note: wrath is fierce anger
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: The threat of furious rage spreading over Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spectre of' reads as 'the threat of', as in the spectre of war, but it is the ghost itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A wraith is a ghost or apparition, especially one seen just before or after a death.

clue.text: Everybody in church welcomes a marriage

indicators.note: to welcome a guest is to take them inside, so one piece is let in among the others

parts.note: everybody is all
taken as written
CE is the Church of England
taken as written

explanation.surface: The whole congregation greets a wedding couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a connecting word placing everybody inside the church, but it supplies two letters of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union by marriage between families, as well as any formal partnership.

clue.text: Tennis trailblazer remains on the phone

indicators.note: on a phone call you hear a voice only, so the word counts by its sound

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A pioneering tennis player is still taking a call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' reads as a verb, stays, but it is the noun for what is left after a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ashe was the first Black man to win Wimbledon and the US Open, breaking barriers in the sport.

clue.text: Is often confused with regard to light

indicators.note: confused things are jumbled, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written
re means concerning or with regard to

explanation.surface: Something is frequently mistaken for something else where lighting is concerned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' at the end looks like a noun, illumination, but it is the verb, to ignite.
explanation.definitionFit: To light a fire or candle is to ignite it, which is to set it ablaze or kindle it.
